newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jailed Indonesian labour leader taken to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Indonesian labour leader taken to hospital.

text.p: Jailed Indonesian labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan, who is on trial for subversion, was taken to hospital on Tuesday, one of his lawyers and family members said.

"Today he was taken to hospital to be examined but it is not clear whether he will be treated or just examined," Bambang Widjojanto, head of the Indonesian Legal Aid Foundation, told Reuters by telephone.
Widjojanto said it was unclear what Pakpahan's problem was.

Pakpahan, head of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI), was detained in July and charged with subversion, which carries the death penalty, following riots in the capital Jakarta on July 27.
Family members contacted at Pakpahan's home in Jakarta said they understood he had been taken to hospital but no details were available on his condition.
Widjojanto said Pakapahan would be taken to the Kramat Jati police hospital in Jakarta where he would be examined by his own doctor in the presence of a member of his legal team.
The International Confederation of Free Trade Unions (ICFTU) last week expressed concern about Pakpahan's medical condition during his detention in Jakarta's Cipinang prison.

"Following various ailments suffered earlier in prison, Brother Pakpahan now complains of a sudden deterioration which may be connected with his known heart condition," ICFTU general secretary Bill Jordan said in a letter to the justice minister last week.

Lawyers said his trial, which began in December, was adjourned on Monday after Pakpahan complained that neither the prison head nor regional officials of the justice department would consent to an examination by his own doctor as allowed under the criminal procedure code.
Pakpahan was jailed in 1994 on charges that he incited racial rioting in the north Sumatran city of Medan in April that year after a series of workers strikes.
He was freed on appeal and his conviction was quashed by the Supreme Court. The conviction was reinstated last year after his arrest on the subversion charge.
